title: Firebase App Distribution (DevOps view)
objectives: Understand Firebase App Distribution from a DevOps perspective
Fit App Distribution into a multi-ring release pipeline
Automate uploads from CI with service-account auth
Manage testers, groups, release notes, symbols

sections.markdown:
**Think of Firebase App Distribution as the office-mailroom that hands out pre-release builds to invited testers — bypassing the store review queue.**

While the store (Play + App Store) takes hours-to-days to review a build, App Distribution delivers it in minutes. Perfect for the fastest ring of your release pipeline: internal QA + designers + PMs who need to poke at every commit's build.

- **Push AAB / APK / IPA to invited tester emails.**
- **No store review.** Delivered via email + tester-app install flow.
- **CI-friendly** — service-account authenticated uploads via Firebase CLI or Actions plugin.
- **Groups + release notes** — target subsets of testers.
- **Tester SDK** — in-app 'new build available' UX.
- **Symbol upload** alongside — Crashlytics needs it.
- **Free** — no per-build/tester cost.

**From a DevOps view:** App Distribution is the FASTEST ring in a well-designed release pipeline. Every push to `main` builds + distributes to `qa` group; every tag builds + distributes to `beta`; only vetted builds promote to Play/TestFlight. **The rule of App Distribution:** it's a fast-feedback ring, NOT a substitute for Play/TestFlight for wider beta.

**Firebase App Distribution** is Google's pre-release distribution service. Uploads AAB/APK/IPA + release notes → invited testers receive email + install via App Distribution mobile app (Android) or ad-hoc-signed provisioning (iOS). Service-account authenticated for CI. Free at any volume. **DevOps role:** the innermost / fastest ring of a mobile release pipeline; complements (not replaces) Play + App Store cadence.

sections.code:
# GitHub Actions job
distribute-android-dev:
  needs: build-android
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
      with: {name: android-aab}
    - uses: wzieba/Firebase-Distribution-Github-Action@v1
      with:
        appId: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID_ANDROID_DEV }}
        serviceCredentialsFileContent: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SA_JSON_DEV }}
        groups: qa,designers
        releaseNotes: |
          Build ${{ github.sha }}
          ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        file: app-release.aab
    - name: upload symbols to Crashlytics
      run: |
        firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload \
          --app ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_APP_ID_ANDROID_DEV }} \
          ./symbols

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Not automating uploads.** Someone forgets → QA has no build.
**Mistake 2: Using App Distribution as prod substitute.** No auto-update; users can't install from store.
**Mistake 3: Missing symbol upload.** Crashes come back obfuscated.
**Mistake 4: Debug build distributed.** Wrong Firebase project + missing obfuscation.
**Mistake 5: Static + broad tester lists.** Ex-employees still get builds.
**Mistake 6: Empty release notes.** Testers ignore anonymous builds.
**Mistake 7: Same App Distribution project across envs.** dev + staging + prod builds land together.
**Mistake 8: Not scoping service-account role.** Overly-privileged CI account.
## Best practices
**1. Every push builds + distributes** to the innermost ring.
**2. Staging Firebase project** — distinct from prod.
**3. Symbols uploaded alongside every build.**
**4. Segmented groups** — qa / designers / internal / beta.
**5. Auto-populated release notes** from git.
**6. Ring cadence:** every-push → nightly → weekly → tag → prod.
**7. Service account minimal role** (Firebase App Distribution Admin only).
**8. Rotate testers** from HR / IdP.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Manual CLI upload to a qa tester group.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — GitHub Actions on push-to-main → distribute to qa.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Symbol upload alongside distribution.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Multi-flavor: dev + staging distinct App Distribution projects.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — In-app Tester SDK for 'new build available' banner.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — HR-synced tester groups via Cloud Function reading Okta.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Where does App Distribution fit in a well-designed release pipeline?**

**A:** **Innermost ring** — the fastest feedback loop between commit + tester. **Every push to `main`** triggers CI build + upload to App Distribution `qa` group; QA can install within minutes. **Nightly** distributes to whole-company `internal` group for dogfooding. **Weekly** promotes to Play Closed + TestFlight External for external beta. **Tag** promotes to Play Internal + TestFlight Internal for release-candidate testing. **Only vetted** builds promote to store production. **App Distribution's role:** speed. Store review takes hours-days; App Distribution takes minutes. **NOT a substitute** for store rings — auto-updates + wider audience require Play/TestFlight. **Interviewer signal:** knowing App Distribution complements, doesn't replace, the store.

**Q2: How does CI service-account auth work for App Distribution?**

**A:** **(1) Create a service account** in Google Cloud IAM with role `Firebase App Distribution Admin` (least privilege). **(2) Download JSON key** — treat as a secret. **(3) Store in CI secret** — GitHub Actions Secrets, Codemagic env-var group, etc. **(4) In pipeline:** Firebase Actions plugin (`wzieba/Firebase-Distribution-Github-Action`) or `firebase appdistribution:distribute` CLI reads the JSON + uploads. **(5) Rotate keys periodically** — 90-day cadence common; immediate on team-member departure. **(6) Scope by env** — separate service accounts per dev/staging/prod Firebase project. **(7) Audit** — Cloud IAM logs every use of the service account. **Interviewer signal:** knowing least-privilege + rotation + per-env isolation.

**Q3: What's the story with the Tester SDK — should you ship it in prod?**

**A:** **NO.** The Tester SDK enables in-app 'new build available; tap to install' — great UX for staging + internal builds. **But:** (1) It bypasses the Play Store / App Store update mechanism. (2) Play Store policies forbid apps auto-updating outside the Play channel. (3) iOS ad-hoc distribution is limited to registered devices. **Practical usage:** flavor-gated. **`dev` and `staging` flavors** include the Tester SDK; **`prod` flavor** excludes it. Use `--dart-define ENV=dev` or build-time conditional imports. **Store submission:** the prod-flavor build has no Tester SDK code paths; passes review cleanly. **Alternative** for prod updates: Firebase Remote Config `min_supported_app_version` → in-app 'update available' banner + deep-link to Play Store. Interviewer signal: understanding the store policy nuance.

**Q4: How do you handle iOS ad-hoc distribution via App Distribution?**

**A:** **iOS is trickier than Android:** ad-hoc builds are signed against a provisioning profile that lists **specific UDIDs**. When a new tester joins: (1) They receive an invite email. (2) Tap → their device installs a Firebase profile that collects UDID. (3) YOU must **re-sign the IPA** with an updated provisioning profile including the new UDID. (4) Upload new IPA. **Automation:** Fastlane `match` + `firebase_app_distribution` plugin can auto-invite testers + regenerate profiles. **Bottleneck:** the re-signing step + upload requires CI to spin up on every new tester addition. **Alternative for iOS:** use **TestFlight for external testers** (no UDID management; Apple handles); reserve App Distribution for internal QA where UDIDs are stable. **Enterprise cert** (paid Apple Enterprise Program) bypasses UDIDs but Apple audits strictly — 'employee-only.' Interviewer signal: recognizing iOS UDID pain + best fallback.

**Q5: How do you keep Firebase App Distribution tester lists clean?**

**A:** **(1) Group by role** — `qa`, `designers`, `internal`, `beta_partners`. Distribute only relevant builds per group. **(2) Sync with HR / IdP** — Cloud Function reads Google Workspace / Okta group membership + updates Firebase tester groups nightly. Ex-employees auto-removed. **(3) Retention policy** — testers inactive for 90 days auto-removed. **(4) External beta groups** — explicit opt-in + periodic re-consent (GDPR). **(5) Audit periodically** — list all testers + verify. **(6) Delete on request** — GDPR right-to-erasure. **(7) Analytics on install rate** — testers who never install → stale. **The manual approach** (spreadsheet) breaks down at any real team size. Interviewer signal: automation + governance.

**Q6: App Distribution vs Play Internal vs TestFlight — how do you pick + can you use them together?**

**A:** **All three coexist in a mature pipeline.** **App Distribution:** fastest (no review) + free unlimited testers + email-based invite. Use for internal QA + designer previews + specific external partners. **Play Internal Testing:** ~2-hour review + AAB signing validation + delivered via Play Store (better UX, auto-updates). Use for release-candidate rings + testing the exact upload path prod uses. **TestFlight Internal:** no review + up to 100 dev-team members (App Store Connect roles) + iOS-only. **TestFlight External:** ~1-day review + up to 10K testers by email or public link. **Best pattern:** internal QA → App Distribution; RC verification → Play Internal + TestFlight Internal; external beta → Play Closed + TestFlight External; prod → Play Prod + App Store. **Interviewer signal:** knowing all three fit different purposes.

## Real-world usage

- **Every mobile team's innermost ring.**
- **Nightly dogfooding.**
- **External partner previews.**
- **NOT for** wide external beta (Play/TestFlight) or prod (store).

## Advanced notes

- **`firebase appdistribution:distribute`** — CLI.
- **`firebase appdistribution:testers:add / remove`** — programmatic.
- **Release TTL** — App Distribution builds live ~30 days.
- **App Distribution API** — REST for custom integrations.
- **Slack + email notifications** on new build.
- **Feedback form** — testers submit screenshots + notes (paid feature).
- **In-app 'update available'** via Tester SDK (flavor-gated).
- **Web dashboard** — release history + install analytics.
- **Multi-project setup** — separate Firebase projects per env.
